Playing for a district, not just taking turns

Firsthand design playtest of the previous release: Grand Harbor, seed 1, eight rounds instead of the usual 26, untimed bidding. I played Seat 1 through the browser against the shipped bots. This was one deliberately short game, not a balance sample.

I turned down $204 for Dry Dock and paid $185 for Slipway. That left me one deed short of Shipyards. Later, I spent $230 on Grain Quay to block Seat 3’s Exchange set. The very next auction was for Spar Yard, the deed I wanted. With $125 left I couldn’t raise the $150 bid. Seat 3 won it for $200.

The best decision wasn’t a dice roll. I traded Grain Quay for Spar Yard and $30. We both completed a district. I risked $30 improving Slipway; nobody landed there. Seat 2 landed on my trading partner’s Tea Wharf instead and paid $106. In net worth Seat 2 won with $1,157, ahead of Seat 3 at $1,023 and me at $880.

What felt flat: the table showed Grain Quay’s list price without telling me it would complete my opponent’s set. The pre-roll desk kept saying “Ready to roll,” even when a mutually useful deal had just become possible. The interesting part was anticipating another player’s move, but the game asked me to reconstruct that from property lists. More animations or extra spaces wouldn’t have fixed that.

The revised helm names missing deeds, the score gap and the rival who stands to complete a set. Trades put both sides on the chart. The remaining limitation is bargaining: a rejection ends the conversation; neither side can counter. That’s the next mechanic worth testing with human opponents, not a change to the rules in this release.

Same decisions in the Rust core

With the same 24 rolls and card draws, my net worth was $880 after the trade and build, $910 after the trade without building, and $920 without either. The bots reacted to the actual holdings in each branch. The swap was interesting even though it did not win this seed.

In 100 full-length Grand Harbor games with three shipped bots, 698 of 698 proposals were accepted; 0 were deed-for-deed offers. The swap I enjoyed making is not one these bots initiate. This measures the controller, not human enjoyment. Reproduce with node tests/playtest.mjs after building.

Desktop interaction and scenario audit

105 interactions · 87 scenarios. The old Activity view hid all balances. The new treasury is independent of the selected instrument; game sheets have their own fixed funds strip. The board and decision dock do not disappear to show portfolios or history.

Desktop mouse paths from the named starting state. Count each deliberate activation, including opening a native select and picking an option (2). Typing, waiting, automatic resolution, and site navigation are excluded and named where relevant. Reading at 0 means no click, hover, scroll, or keyboard shortcut. Decisions with several participants count each participant’s clicks. Repeated bids and edits add their own costs. Budgets are ceilings, not an instruction to remove safeguards.

What still takes effort: from Manage deeds, choosing a nondefault build and confirming takes three clicks including entry, down from four via the old select. Selecting the desired buildable tile directly skips the entry click. Changing a map and one controller costs seven clicks from play; these infrequent controls stay out of quick start. Leaving an active network match costs three: the last confirmation protects every device. Budgets measure effort, not enjoyment; they are not human playtest results.

Read a district from the whole deed

District identity belongs to the tile face, not its header. With color and the top third excluded, the middle and lower face must still carry the district’s recognizable print. Names and values must remain legible on that print. Check every shipped map and the folded phone board, including intervening service spaces. Ownership and trade selections must not erase the print. A complete set must be readable without opening a portfolio, and its mark must disappear when the set breaks.

Ignore the top third and remove color. On each remaining third, the browser checks for visible engraving around the title, excluding prices, stamps and ship pieces. The combined samples must match their own named print more closely than any other. This includes both legs of a pending trade and a complete set. A header stripe cannot pass. Compare the faces.

Show why this decision matters now

When a deed is one player's last missing district member, an offer or auction must name that player and the rent at stake before the commitment, even if it is a rival. Before rolling, identify an almost complete district's missing deed and owner without a portfolio lookup. Show the real net-worth gap on a scored table; cash is not the score.

Read the result; never tidy it away

The next turn must be playable while a letter still shows its recipient, instruction and actual effect. Allow a six-second read without input, on desktop and a muted reduced-motion phone. Then reclaim the chart automatically. One visit to Activity must recover the exact result, even after rejoin. Filing is not a game command and must not pause a bid clock.

The browser observes the text for six seconds across handoff on each device, takes the next turn and checks that the letter clears without input. Activity recovers the same recipient, bill and cash afterward. See the letters.

Position is not ownership

At rest, distinguish the owner of the occupied deed, the visiting ship and the owner's actual location without navigating, scrolling, hovering or relying on color. Test a visitor on a rival deed when the owner is somewhere else, plus several ships sharing a berth.

Board target and consequence visibility

When a command targets deeds, mark the actual spaces and show cash and district effects before commitment. A board click selects, never spends or transfers. For trades, distinguish give, get, other owners and locked districts; reverse the viewpoint for the recipient and show both balances, sets made or broken and any lost refit. Test nondefault targets, refusal and both desktop and folded boards. Counting clicks alone is not a pass.

Trades were in the click inventory, but not in this criterion. The old modal passed without showing a single target. The build now requires every deed-targeting Rust command, including the proposal payload and its responses, to appear in a linked scenario. See the two-sided trade.

Palette and measured contrast

Navy surrounds the controls, cream is the reading surface, amber marks action and selection. Seat numbers, underlines, signed amounts and labeled buttons also carry meaning without color. Ratios use rendered CSS pairs for flat surfaces. For tile titles, the review hides only the lettering and measures the worst pixel behind each name on Grand Harbor. This is not a whole-app accessibility certification. The guardrails are 4.5:1 for sampled text and 3:1 for the focus outline.

Watch a turn, with sound

An actual local game: Seat 1 rolls, opens Copper Yard to bids, and wins it for $10 when Seat 2 withdraws. The rattling dice, bid and closing gavel are recorded from the game.

Interaction review checklist

Visual priorities, commands and non-game interactions

Space identifiers

1 · Destination
Name stays legible at all times. A gold frame means inspected; the ship markers show actual occupants.
2 · Decision value
Print the deed name over a light engraving and put only its price, rent or action quote on a small plain ticket. Service spaces use a dark face with a service symbol and a written effect instead.
District membership versus a full set
The whole deed is printed in its district’s color and motif. Even without the top third, a member should match its siblings in grayscale. The perimeter key and folded tile names spell out the district. A double frame and SET stamp mean a single seat owns the set; a DEED ribbon names that seat. Neither mark means a ship is here or a trade has been agreed.
3 · Ownership versus presence
A permanent DEED number identifies the owner even when their ship is elsewhere. The numbered ship pieces below the price are the current visitors. Fleet station always names every ship’s berth, balance and who owns its space.
4 · Detail on demand
Inspector and accessible label carry district, level, precise amounts and full effects. Never rely on color or sound alone.
Property map · eligibility and consequence
A hollow diamond and signed quote mark each candidate; a check identifies the selected deed. Show affected district members separately from the clicked member. See the board-target-preview criterion in the interaction and scenario audit.

Accepted commands

  • Start or rematch: Fresh board; no startup fanfare · sound: quiet
  • Roll and land: Dice tumble to their actual faces; the numbered ship traces its route. The destination and net cash change stay on the table. · sound: dice
  • Purchase a deed: Deed seal lands, tile receives an ink stamp, buyer’s balance shows the debit. · sound: coin
  • Open bidding: Announce the auction · sound: gavel
  • Raise bid: Confirm the accepted amount · sound: bid
  • Withdraw or expire: Bidder leaves the lot, or gavel closes with winner and actual price. No sale has a separate result. · sound: down
  • Develop property: Hammer strikes; every improved tile gets its level stamp, with cost and new rent or district scope on the table. · sound: build
  • Sell to the bank: Review proceeds and rent surrendered before returning the deed to market. · sound: coin
  • Sell improvements to cover debt: Remove the quoted levels, credit the original bill and show any debt or cash left. · sound: sale
  • Declare bankruptcy: Confirm before returning all remaining deeds; remove the debtor’s ship from play. · sound: down
  • Commission works: Stamp the property that receives the project; the ship stays at the works. · sound: build
  • Decline works: Keep the cash instead of commissioning a project. · sound: down
  • Send proposal: Show the same marked properties and terms from the recipient's side. No assets move yet. · sound: paper
  • Accept contract: Transfer both legs together; mark any completed districts. · sound: coin
  • Decline contract: Return to proposer · sound: down
  • Take guild grant: Confirm cash payment · sound: coin
  • Choose rent cover: Confirm cover · sound: bell
  • Advance turn: Ordinary transitions are quiet; final scores get a cadence · sound: quiet

Other interactions

  • Inspect / browse: Select a tile with pointer or keyboard; check focus vs landing, name, cost and owner.
  • Players / activity / rules: Desktop keeps the board and command dock visible. Switch the right instrument, inspect a named holding or return to the offered lot. Phone switches views.
  • Treasury: Check every seat without a click, scroll, or hover on all instruments and inside game sheets. For path costs, budgets and contrast evidence see review/clicks.json and review/desktop.py.
  • Local setup: Check solo, pass-and-play, custom seats, map, policy and clock before replacing a game.
  • Online setup: Host, join by code, copy invite, assign seats and launch. Guests cannot change the rules.
  • Network recovery: Pause on disconnect. Rehost, rejoin, cancel or forget; historical commands must remain silent.
  • Bidding: Check presets, exact entry, insufficient cash, timer pause/expiry and final sale.
  • Rent / fee / card: A live dispatch shows the instruction and actual effect through the handoff, then clears itself. Activity keeps the exact receipt, including after rejoin. No acknowledgement, sound or animation is needed to play or understand a draw.
  • Victory and debt: Choose net worth at the round limit or last solvent merchant. During an unresolved bill, preview deed or level sales, or explicitly declare bankruptcy even when sale proceeds could cover the bill.
  • Guild / exchange / works: Distinguish the visiting ship from the deed under auction or receiving a project; make both sides of each offer explicit.
  • Local presentation: Open Display settings, choose the visual pace on this device only. Keep the operating system’s reduced-motion preference and bid clock independent of presentation.
  • Trading: Draft on the actual board, not in a separate form. Distinguish your deed, the requested deed, other partners and nontradable spaces without color. Preview both cash balances and both districts before sending or accepting. Declining or cancelling must not transfer assets. See the board-target-preview scenarios.
  • Manage deeds / public works: Select the actual deed, not a menu entry. Compare Improve and Sell without leaving the map. Show all engine-quoted candidates, the selected deed, cash afterward and the effect of confirming. Selection, mode switching and cancellation must never issue a game command.
  • Audio / motion: Local foley starts after user interaction unless muted. Reduced motion keeps the settled dice, outcome and balance changes without a moving pawn, stamp or ripple. Review with review/motion.py.
  • Results / leave: Show winners and scores. Rematch locally or explicitly end the network table.

Desktop playtest review

Before: one offer, three reading locations

Inspect capture

The previous layout repeated the space name in the chart, inspector and footer. Buying meant leaving the economics at the upper right for a button at the opposite end of the screen. The folded chart was hard to follow as a circuit.

Before: laptop table

Inspect capture

The treasury was a child of the board. Opening Activity hid both the board and every balance. The small green-gray labels also gave little separation between status and controls.

After: chart → decision → details

Inspect capture

At 1366 × 768 the ship travels a continuous perimeter. A single right rail asks “Buy or auction?”, puts both commitments immediately below their amounts, and keeps the selected deed’s ladder underneath. The treasury stays fixed.

After: read the log

Inspect capture

Activity changes only the right instrument. The board and current commands stay in place; reading the treasury costs zero clicks.

After: timed auction

Inspect capture

Bidder, next commitment, time remaining and all cash balances remain visible. Inspecting the lot is not a bid.

Read the table in play

Whose ship, and whose deed?

Inspect capture

Seat 2 is on Silk Arcade; its DEED 1 ribbon belongs to Seat 1, whose ship is at Port Office. Fleet station spells out both locations without hovering. Select a berth name to locate that ship without changing the chosen deed.

Read it now or later

Inspect capture

Fogbound cargo charged Seat 1 $55. Passing Port Office earned $240. The letter separates both amounts while Seat 2 plays, then leaves the chart on its own. Activity keeps the exact receipt.

Read through a handoff

Inspect capture

Muted and reduced motion: the card still names its recipient and displays $65 of cover, with the next player’s roll available underneath.

Presentation, per device

Inspect capture

Standard separates the cast, the journey and the landing. Fast shortens presentation; reduced motion uses the same final result. This is not a host rule and does not change the five-second clock.

Roll and travel

Inspect capture

The dice settle to the Rust result and the numbered ship moves clockwise. The arrival and price remain readable after motion stops.

Hammer falls

Inspect capture

The lot is stamped and the ledger debits the winner, not the player who withdrew. The next decision is available separately.

Reduced-motion phone

Inspect capture

Same seeded arrival, with stationary dice, a pinned result and a larger three-column route. Muting does not remove any information.

Set up a table

Mode picker

Inspect capture

Keep the four play modes visible. Common local games start immediately; customization is secondary.

Local settings

Inspect capture

Board and clock apply to the whole table; seat selectors choose the controllers. A future improvement is a short roster summary before Start.

Join by code

Inspect capture

One input accepts a typed or pasted six-character code. Explicit submission lets players correct it before connecting.

Host lobby

Inspect capture

Keep the invitation code beside Copy. Connected devices receive seats automatically, with individual overrides for shared devices.

Guest waiting room

Inspect capture

Identify the table and joining device. Showing the guest their provisional seat assignments before launch would reduce uncertainty.

Interrupted table

Inspect capture

Distinguish a paused network table from a completed match. A returning device needs a recovery action, not a fresh local game.

Navigate and inspect

Eight districts without their headers

Inspect capture

For each district: a full deed on the left, a different member on the right with color and the top third removed. These are enlarged crops of the actual board, not drawings of the intended tile.

A set, not just a color

Inspect capture

After the trade, a double frame and SET stamp mark all six Shipyards and Exchange deeds. The DEED ribbons still identify two different owners; the numbered ship at Grain Quay is a visitor.

Follow the printed faces

Inspect capture

All 24 Grand Harbor deeds carry their engraving across the board space. Bottle Post interrupts the brickwork of Old Town with a dark envelope face: a draw, not a deed.

Full names on the folded route

Inspect capture

Three Old Town deeds share the same brickwork and full district name. The deed title sits directly on the print; a small plain ticket keeps the price distinct. No legend lookup or tap is required.

Four visitors on an improved deed

Inspect capture

Density fixture: the deed ribbon is separate from all four numbered ship markers. Nobody disappears into an anonymous count; the inspector keeps the development ladder.

Grand Harbor circuit

Inspect capture

The 40-space circuit distinguishes guilds, dispatches, exchanges, fees and deed districts. Inspect a space to read its effect.

Pocket chart

Inspect capture

On small devices the larger circuit becomes a scrollable route in movement order. The desktop perimeter is not shrunk to fit a phone.

Purchase decision on desktop

Inspect capture

The landed deed opens beside the board. See every tier’s construction cost, total rent and incremental payoff before buying or opening an auction.

Board, turns and balances

Inspect capture

Keep movement and cash visible together on desktop. The decision dock stays available when switching views on a phone.

Deed inspection

Inspect capture

The owner or market status now comes first; price, base rent and full-district rent are aligned for comparison.

Player portfolios

Inspect capture

Show cash and district counts together. Choose a named holding to inspect it directly.

Activity feed

Inspect capture

Keep history newest-first and available without dismissing the turn. Round dividers would make long matches easier to scan.

Rulebook

Inspect capture

Keep rules one tap away without leaving the table. The decision dock carries the immediate action rather than requiring a rulebook lookup.

Make a market decision

The opponent’s reason to bid

Inspect capture

Seat 3 already owns Fish Hall and Tea Wharf. Buying Grain Quay blocks their set; putting it up for auction gives them a shot at $116 rent. The offer tells you before you choose.

Deed offer

Inspect capture

Show the cash left after purchase alongside rent. Bid at auction remains a distinct alternative to buying at list price.

Timed bid

Inspect capture

A shrinking bar and numeric countdown show the remaining window; the last two seconds change color. Keep bid presets and withdrawal reachable without a keyboard.

Custom bid

Inspect capture

Show the legal range before numeric entry. A custom bid never commits until submitted; online, the host clock still applies.

Bidder handoff

Inspect capture

Keep the leader and acting seat separate. The amount on each bid button is the actual commitment, not an increment.

Two districts, one draft

Inspect capture

Grain Quay for Spar Yard completes Exchange and Shipyards. The suggested swap balances the printed values with $40. Either player’s stake is visible before a proposal is sent. Select another actual tile to change the deal.

The same deal, from the other chair

Inspect capture

The proposer changed the premium to $30. GIVE and GET flip to the recipient’s perspective, while the deed flags still identify their current owners. Accept and Decline are separate from reading.

Review on the folded chart

Inspect capture

The same proposed assets are marked on the phone route. Cash and district effects live with the decision; the original owner keeps the deed until acceptance.

Settle the game

Sell a deed or declare bankruptcy

Inspect capture

The debtor owes $40. Selling Copper Yard nets $70: the creditor gets $40 and the debtor keeps $30. Declaring bankruptcy instead requires explicit confirmation.

Settlement

Inspect capture

Show the outcome, then advance automatically. The activity feed preserves results that go by too quickly.

Final accounts

Inspect capture

Show the winner and each seat’s net worth. Local rematch reuses settings instead of reopening setup.

Develop a district

Sell a different deed

Inspect capture

Each saleable deed shows the bank’s payout on the actual tile. Selecting Silk Arcade quotes its cash and forfeited rent; the board also shows the fall in rent on the rest of the set.

One-use refit

Inspect capture

The same board picker previews a refit on Dry Dock while the ship stays at Dock Works. No rival visit means no payoff.

Build or hold

Inspect capture

Diamond marks give every available construction price; the check identifies the selected deed. Compare its rent before and after without leaving the map. Cancel spends nothing.

Whole-district quote

Inspect capture

Selecting any sibling previews the same project. Dashed outlines mark the other deeds that will improve; the map shows each one’s rent before and after, for one combined construction price.

Board targeting on a phone

Inspect capture

The folded board scrolls independently above the quote. Tap a deed or step between candidates; cash, the actual outcome, and the confirmation stay in reach.

After construction

Inspect capture

The deed shows its current rent, level cap and why its next level is blocked. District lock and investment are also visible in the portfolio.
